drafts.passage: Thornbill-NER met the pre-specified robustness criterion (drop ≤ 2.0 points) at all tested noise rates, with mean test F1 drops of 0.6, 1.3, and 1.8 points at 10%, 20%, and 30% label noise, respectively. In contrast, Lindgren-Tagger failed the criterion at every noise rate, with drops of 2.6, 5.5, and 8.9 points at 10%, 20%, and 30% noise, respectively. Thornbill-NER also maintained a higher mean F1 than Lindgren-Tagger under all noise conditions, with the advantage growing from 2.6 points at 10% noise to 4.8 points at 20% and 7.7 points at 30%. On original labels, Thornbill-NER achieved a slightly higher mean F1 (91.4 ± 0.4) and a smaller seed range (0.9 points) than Lindgren-Tagger (90.8 ± 0.5, range 1.2), though no statistical test was reported for these differences.
